$comment: What holds for each specification under spec/; its form is spec/status.schema.json. The texts under spec/*.md are frozen at the casting named here and are not edited, apart from the status block at their top. scripts/build-spec-status.mjs writes that block, the status section of README.md and the document table of apps/site/src/content/docs/reference/specifications.md from this file; `npm run validate` checks them with --check, and checks each frozen text against its `textDigest`. `statements` is the source of the marked statements about what the library builds today on README.md, the site and the direction notes; the generator writes them into the places marked <!-- now:<id> -->. A part that is built, partly built or built differently names its `evidence` in the library, the vectors or the ceremony definitions. Where a text and the library disagree, the library with its vectors and flows holds until the text is brought up to date.

statuses.partly-built: implemented in the library in part; a note names what is not built, or `differences` points to where the differences are documented
statuses.built-differently: implemented in the library with a reading other than the text; `differences` points to where it is documented: a row of lib/DEVIATIONS.md, the header of a source file, a test
statuses.direction-changed: the planned model differs from the text; `direction` names the direction note
statuses.not-verified: no evidence was checked for this part

groups.short: The library and the app run a membership log replicated among the members, with founding, admission and leaving; removal, rule changes, epoch transitions and key changes are not built ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).
groups.long: The library runs stage 1 of the group log: founding, admission by invitation and acceptance, and leaving, with the log exchanged along the invitation edges. Removal (`member.remove`), rule changes, epoch transitions, device cards and the conflict rules for removal and rule changes are not built ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).

group-keys.short: In the library, epoch transitions, key rotation and removal are not built ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).
group-keys.long: The library builds neither key distribution nor key state transitions such as rotation; its group log uses the exchange and ingest admission of Replication §4.4 and §7, without a registered replication adapter ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).

key-states.short: In the library no removal, rotation or rule change starts a key state, because none of them is built.

linear.short: The library founds a group under `linear/0.1`; it does not build the key delivery.

group-rules.short: In the library, changing the rules (`policy.change`) is not built.

group-leave.short: In the library today a member can leave, and the leave takes effect in the log at once; a leave by the last member ends the group. Removal is not built, and no new key epoch follows a leave or a lost device, so the library does not make later content unreadable to whoever left.

device-cards.short: In the library, device cards are not built: one device per person.

group-conflicts.short: In the library, two admissions of the same person made at the same time both stand and make one member. A leave at the same time as an admission of the same person, a case these rules leave open, is read as the leave winning. Removals and rule changes, and their collisions, are not built.

vouch-threshold.short: the library founds a group only with a vouch threshold of 1 and changes no rule afterwards.

member-remove.short: In the library a member leaves by a `member.leave`; `member.remove` and epoch transitions are not built ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).

welcome.short: The library sends its own `x-membership-welcome/0.1` in place of `access-operation/0.1`, and the new member fetches the log ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).

access-task-types.short: The library carries the schemas of `key-delivery/0.1` and `removal-notice/0.1` but sends and receives neither: key distribution and `member.remove` are not built ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).

encounter-ceremony.short: The app connects people with `shared-connect` instead, defined in [`interop/ceremonies/`](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/tree/main/interop/ceremonies).
encounter-ceremony.long: `encounter-scan`, the ceremony of the Encounter Layer, is superseded: the Web of Trust app connects people with `shared-connect` instead ([web-of-trust#555](https://github.com/real-life-org/web-of-trust/pull/555), [`apps/wot-v3/src/adapters/rltp/index.ts`](https://github.com/real-life-org/web-of-trust/blob/af18d3df0e02b1b924df9670076c63b6195f2857/apps/wot-v3/src/adapters/rltp/index.ts#L60-L65)). It is defined in [`interop/ceremonies/`](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/tree/main/interop/ceremonies) with its vector and implemented as holder acts in the library; no specification text describes it yet ([status](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/spec/status.json)).

app-profile.short: The Web of Trust app connects people with `shared-connect`, whose steps use the public Trust Tasks `vrc/relationships/propose/0.1` and `vrc/relationships/issue/0.1`, with their `#response` documents, and a decline is a [`trust-task-error`](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/lib/src/shared-connect.ts#L633) ([definition](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/interop/ceremonies/shared-connect.ceremony.json), [vector](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/vectors/shared-connect.json)).
app-profile.long: The Web of Trust app connects people with `shared-connect`: the inviter shows a code or sends a link; the steps use the public Trust Tasks `vrc/relationships/propose/0.1` and `vrc/relationships/issue/0.1`, with their `#response` documents, and a decline is a [`trust-task-error`](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/lib/src/shared-connect.ts#L633); the credential each side issues is a DTG `RelationshipCredential` with two contexts, W3C credentials v2 and the DTG registry context v1 ([definition](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/interop/ceremonies/shared-connect.ceremony.json), [vector](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/vectors/shared-connect.json), [app](https://github.com/real-life-org/web-of-trust/blob/af18d3df0e02b1b924df9670076c63b6195f2857/apps/wot-v3/src/adapters/rltp/index.ts#L60-L65)).

identity.short: With the library's default key provider `seedKeys`, the person's anchors are derived from a root seed given as bytes, which the Identity Layer text (§4) derives from the words; each anchor is a `did:key`, and an app may bind another key provider.
identity.long: The library's seed key provider derives a person's long-lived anchor keys from one root seed. Each anchor context (a relationship, a group, a persona) has its own key, derived from the seed and the context's label, and the context's identifier is a `did:key` of that key; device keys are derived per device within an anchor context.

derived-identities.short: The service identity derivation of Identity §7 is not built; for a group's founding the library uses a provisional derivation ([D3](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/lib/DEVIATIONS.md)).
derived-identities.long: The library builds the carrier identity and a provisional service identity ([D3](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/lib/DEVIATIONS.md)), not the recovery context.

holder.short: One holder holds one identity: two stores over one root seed hold two states that never reconcile, so a second device or a second app of the same person cannot hold that identity yet ([`lib/README.md`, "The holder"](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/lib/README.md#the-holder)).

continuity.short: In the library a re-encounter is chained into the existing relationship once the counterpart's continuity mapping verifies; two re-encounters at the same time can leave the chaining one-sided, each side keeping unchained a new relationship the other side chained. Details: the header of [`lib/src/trust/continuity.ts`](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/lib/src/trust/continuity.ts).

direction-assumptions.short: the library's default key provider `seedKeys` follows the second and the third for the person's anchors; it takes the seed as bytes and does not check that they come from words.

recovery.short: Recovering a whole identity from the mnemonic and a copy of the person's state is specified, not built in the library.
recovery.long: The library implements neither the recovery derivation nor the recovery of a whole identity from the words and a copy of its state, nor the synchronization of that state; it does implement the recovery of a lost carrier entry. A holder continues a person's state over the store that holds it and with access to the same keys, with `seedKeys` the same root seed; a holder over an empty store starts a new state.

personas.short: The library derives a persona's anchor from its `persona/<name>` label; no holder act creates or uses a persona.

direction-identity.short: An identifier that survives a key change, linked devices and guardians are planned, not in the library.
direction-identity.long: The library has neither identifiers with a log nor linked devices, generated personal keys or guardians.

vti-adapter.short: The library implements this adapter; the wire binding under `binding/` has live probes against a public development instance of the mediator.

login-identity.short: The library's experimental login identity ([D6](https://github.com/real-life-org/trust-protocol/blob/main/lib/DEVIATIONS.md)) is replaced at stage 3.

parts.note: The library checks only that `replyTo` has the form of a UUID. That it names an earlier message of the same relationship is the sending application's to ensure; the library keeps no history of sent messages to check it against.

parts.title: Holding a message until its tuple is ready
parts.note: `sendMessage` answers `not-ready`; keeping the message until it can be sent is the application's task.

parts.title: Sending, with the sender lifetime (rule 5110)
parts.note: The sender lifetime is a local give-up time on the outbox entry, not a field of the document. For a message the counterpart does not hold, the library's retry horizon of at most P90D ends first, as `failed(expired-by-adapter-policy)`, so the engine's outcome `failed(task-expired)` is unreachable for `message/0.1`; an entry with `held: true` is given up at neither.
